write.heading: Start with a real attempt
write.body: This short function comes from the committed Two Sum demonstration. Run the recorded test to see where its state goes wrong.

run.heading: The result tells us what failed
run.body: The function found two indices, but it reused the same array position.

explore.step: Python is about to execute line {line}. Follow the values as the recorded trace advances.
explore.bug: Both pointers are on index 0. The function adds the first value to itself and accepts an invalid pair.

improve.heading: Now the bug has a shape
improve.body: The failed result was only the symptom. The replay reveals the state that caused it, so the next edit can be deliberate.
improve.insight: Prevent the two pointers from selecting the same index before accepting a match.

narrative.title: A result shows the failure. A trace reveals the cause.
narrative.body: TraceCode connects the active line, the values in memory and the learner’s own reasoning. The error stops being mysterious and becomes a state you can inspect.
narrative.visualLabel: The recorded Two Sum state where both pointers target index zero
narrative.explanation: i and j are both 0, so the value 3 is added to itself.

loop.title: From first attempt to a better mental model.
loop.body: Each stage keeps the learner in control while exposing only the information needed for the next decision.

closing.title: Your code is already telling a story. Learn to read it.
closing.body: Start with one small problem and see every state change that leads to the result.
